records.summary: Article 11 of Timor-Leste's Petroleum Fund Law (Law No. 9/2005 of 3 August, republished with amendments by Law No. 12/2011 of 28 September) puts the Petroleum Fund in government hands and leaves the central bank executing. Article 11(1) says the Government is responsible for the overall management of the Fund. Article 11(2) says the Minister of Finance takes the decisions on the Fund's investment strategy and management, after first seeking the opinion of the Investment Advisory Board under Article 16. Article 11(3) says the Minister signs a contract with the Central Bank (in the 2011 text, with the 'Operational Manager', defined in Article 2(i) as the Central Bank) for the operational management of the Fund, and that the manager is answerable to the Government for that management. Article 16(1)(b) has the Advisory Board advise the Minister on the investment instructions the Minister gives the Fund's investment managers, and Article 2(h) counts the Operational Manager itself as an investment manager, so the instructions run to the bank. Article 12(5) requires the investment manager to act within any instructions issued by the Minister and within the operational management contract. The law is still the one in force in this version: Ministerial Diploma No. 4/2019 of 1 March 2019, published in the Jornal da Republica, cites Law No. 9/2005 'na redacao dada pela Lei n.o 12/2011' and names the Fund's Operational Manager as the Banco Central de Timor-Leste. The arrangement covers the Petroleum Fund only; the law says nothing about who sets interest rates or monetary policy.
records.source_title: Lei n.o 9/2005, de 3 de Agosto - Lei do Fundo Petrolifero, Jornal da Republica (Ministerio da Justica official journal)
records.quote: Artigo 11.o - Gestao do Fundo Petrolifero. 1. O Governo e responsavel pela gestao global do Fundo Petrolifero. 2. records.summary: On 1 March 2019 Timor-Leste's Ministry of Finance published Ministerial Diploma No. 4/2019 in the Jornal da Republica, Serie I No. 8 B, setting the rules and criteria for investing 5 per cent of the Petroleum Fund under Article 15(4) of the Petroleum Fund Law. The preamble records that the Government had decided that the Fund's investments in petroleum operations would be carried out by the state oil company TIMOR GAP - Timor Gas & Petroleo, E.P., under an investment management contract to be signed between the Fund's Operational Manager, named in the text as the Banco Central de Timor-Leste, and that state company. The Council of Ministers approved Government Resolution No. 10/2019 of 27 February 2019 agreeing to the rules, which the Minister of Finance then issued. The diploma is an instance of the standing Article 11 arrangement in use: the Government decided where the money goes and the central bank, as Operational Manager, is the party that signs and executes the contract.

records.summary: In January 2025 a group of members of the Assembly of North Macedonia tabled a bill to amend the Law on the National Bank of the Republic of North Macedonia under the shortened procedure. Article 2 of the bill rewrites Article 15 of that Law so that, within four months of the end of the financial year, the National Bank Council distributes the financial result as follows: 30 per cent to general reserves until the level of base capital under Article 12(1) is reached, then 15 per cent after that level is reached, 'and 2) the remainder to the Budget of the Republic of North Macedonia', and adds that the Bank's income may be distributed only in that way. Article 1 deletes special reserves from Article 13(1) and deletes Article 13(4) altogether. Article 3 deletes point 9-a) from the National Bank Council's powers in Article 47(1). Article 4 orders the Bank to transfer the special reserves it had formed under the old Article 13(4), an amount the bill's explanatory part puts at almost 27 million euro, to the general reserves account within 30 days of the law coming into force, and bars the Bank from using those special reserves in the meantime. The bill's own reasoning says the aim is to raise the Bank's general reserves from 11 to 39 million euro. This is filed as an attempt because the bill text was found but not the enacted gazette text: the National Bank's own website names its current law file 'Zakon za Narodnata banka 16-25', which is consistent with publication in Sluzben vesnik 16/25, but that file and the Bank's whole site answer 403 to automated requests and the enactment could not be read.
records.source_title: Predlog na zakon za izmenuvanje na Zakonot za Narodnata banka na Republika Severna Makedonija, po skratena postapka, Skopje, januari 2025 (proposers: group of MPs)

refused.what_was_read: Three searches, including two extended ones, over Namibian press (The Namibian, Republikein, The Brief, NBC, Windhoek Observer), the National Assembly order papers for September and October 2026 returned by search, and the Bank of Namibia Act 1 of 2020 as held on namiblii.org and lac.org.na. refused.fact_that_would_reverse_it: A dated report - Namibian press, a National Assembly order paper or Hansard, an Auditor-General report, or a Bank of Namibia annual report note - showing a Minister of Finance actually directing the Auditor-General to investigate the Bank of Namibia's accounts or affairs under section 66(2) of the Bank of Namibia Act 1 of 2020. notes: TIMOR-LESTE, the answer to the question asked: the article is Article 11 of Law No. 9/2005 of 3 August (Lei do Fundo Petrolifero), republished with amendments by Law No. 12/2011 of 28 September. Official Portuguese wording of the 2005 text, from mj.gov.tl/jornal: '1. O Governo e responsavel pela gestao global do Fundo Petrolifero. 2. O Ministro nao tomara quaisquer decisoes relativas a estrategia de investimento e a gestao do Fundo Petrolifero sem primeiro obter o parecer do Comite de Assessoria para o Investimento nos termos do artigo 16.o. 3. O Ministro celebrara um contrato com o Banco Central para efeitos da gestao operacional do Fundo Petrolifero e o Banco Central sera responsavel pela gestao operacional do Fundo Petrolifero.' In the 2011 version Article 11(3) reads, in La'o Hamutuk's unofficial English translation, 'The Minister contracts with the Operational Manager for the operational management of the Petroleum Fund, which will be responsible to the Government for such management', and Article 2(i) defines Operational Manager as 'the Central Bank or other public entity created by Act of Parliament which is given responsibility for operational management of the Petroleum Fund'. The Minister's power to issue investment instructions is in Article 12(5) ('quaisquer instrucoes emitidas pelo Ministro') read with Article 16(1)(b) and the Article 2(h) definition that makes the Operational Manager an Investment Manager.

TIMOR-LESTE, still in force: Ministerial Diploma No. 4/2019, published in the Jornal da Republica Serie I No. 8 B on 1 March 2019, cites the Petroleum Fund Law 'na redacao dada pela Lei n.o 12/2011, de 28 de setembro' and names the Fund's Operational Manager as the Banco Central de Timor-Leste. No later amendment to Article 11 was found. The 2019 gazette issues returned by search touch Article 15(4) only.

TIMOR-LESTE, scope limit, written so a later round does not overstate it: Article 11 concerns the Petroleum Fund. It does not say the Government or the Minister decides monetary policy, exchange rate policy or interest rates, and nothing was read on the BCTL's own organic law. Record 1 should not be read as a power over monetary policy.

NORTH MACEDONIA, how to strengthen the record filed: the bill text is hosted by the Economic Chamber of North Macedonia (mchamber.mk), not by the official gazette, which is why weak_source is set true. The document itself is the bill as submitted, with 'PREDLAGACI: Grupa pratenici' (proposers: a group of MPs) on its face and 'Skopje, januari 2025 godina' as its date, and it cites the Law's gazette history as 158/10, 64/12, 123/12, 43/14, 153/15, 6/16, 83/18, 110/21 and 74/24 - which places it before 16/25. The National Bank's own site names its current law file '16-25'. If a hand check confirms 16/25 is this amendment, change the kind from 'attempted law change' to 'law change', set the date to the 16/25 publication date and swap the source for the gazette.

NORTH MACEDONIA, what is NOT in the record: no power of direction over the bank and no at-will dismissal power was found, because the enacted and consolidated law texts could not be read. The record covers the claim on the bank's profit and the legislative order to move its special reserves only.

SAMOA, a possible strengthening of the existing record, not filed as a correction because the Act was not enacted: the existing record rests on the Central Bank of Samoa's letter to the Attorney-General's office. PMN, 19 August 2026, adds a sourced later step - the Central Bank of Samoa Amendment Bill 2026 reached its second reading in Parliament, and the report sets out what it would do: the Governor keeps a six-year term but stops chairing the board, an independent non-executive director becomes chair, the Executive Committee gives the Finance Minister quarterly reports on policy formulation and implementation, and the Minister receives the Bank's draft annual budget with 14 working days to comment while the Board keeps final approval. The same report says the Bill would bar monetary, exchange-rate, supervisory or financial-stability disagreements as grounds for dismissal and would require an independent panel to investigate before Cabinet can recommend removal. Former Prime Minister Fiame Naomi Mata'afa said of it, 'It's clear in the bill the reach being given to the minister of finance', and Prime Minister Laaulialemalietoa Leuatea Polataivao Schmidt told MPs, 'The CBS belongs to the government of Samoa.' The IMF raised concerns in March 2026. On this map's rules the quarterly reports and the 14-day budget comment are accountability provisions, not direction, so the part of the Bill that would matter here is the dismissal grounds and the Cabinet removal route, and none of it is law yet. Source: https://pmn.co.nz/read/political/samoa-moves-to-separate-central-bank-governor-from-board-chair
